correctness.rationale: For a distinguished rooted chord enclosing 2k points and leaving 2(n−1−k) outside, isolation is equivalent to no crossing of the two arcs; conditional independent matchings make EX=[C(k,2)+C(n−1−k,2)]/3. Root symmetry multiplies by n, while unconditional EX=n(n−1)/6; subtracting gives a strictly negative sum with summand n−1+k(n−1−k). End terms k=0,n−1 are circularly adjacent chords and yield -2n(n−1)/(3(2n−1)); k=1,n−2 give the non-simple -1/3 limit, with remaining terms O(1/n) in covariance via geometric-ratio bounds. Independently generated all perfect matchings and rational covariances for n=2 through 6; exact concordance including equality only at n=2. Separate finite checks are not used as the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The two natural statistics of a random chord intersection graph, its isolated-vertex count and edge count, have a novel exact dependence law. The surprising nonvanishing -1/3 covariance correction from chords whose expected count tends to zero is a substantial probabilistic refinement, not recoverable by replacing all isolates with simple chords.

final_claim: For uniform perfect matchings of 2n circular endpoints, n>=2, Cov(I_n,X_n)= -n/(3(2n-1)!!) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1}(2k-1)!!(2n-2k-3)!!(n-1+k(n-1-k)), with exact simple-chord covariance and nonsimple corrections E(I-S)=1/(2n)+O(n^-2), Cov(I-S,X)=-1/3+O(n^-1).
limitations: Uniform labeled cyclic matching only; not arbitrary nonuniform circle graphs.
Root counting and tail bounds, not finite enumeration, support the all-n theorem.
